claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Cyprus
claims.summary: An Ottoman army took Cyprus from Venice, capturing Nicosia and Famagusta and beginning more than three centuries of Ottoman rule that settled a Muslim Turkish-Cypriot community on the island.

sources.label: Cyprus: A Country Study

claims.title: Emergence of the Turkish-Cypriot community
claims.summary: Muslim settlers, many from Anatolia, established a distinct Turkish-Cypriot community alongside the Greek-Cypriot majority, while the Orthodox Church regained authority over Greek Cypriots under the millet system.

claims.title: British administration of Cyprus begins
claims.summary: Under the Cyprus Convention the Ottoman Empire transferred the administration of Cyprus to Britain, which annexed the island in 1914 and made it a Crown colony in 1925.

sources.label: Cyprus: A Country Study

claims.title: EOKA campaign for enosis
claims.summary: The guerrilla organisation EOKA, backed by Archbishop Makarios, fought British rule in pursuit of enosis (union with Greece); Turkish Cypriots opposed enosis and called for taksim (partition).

claims.title: Zürich and London agreements
claims.summary: Britain, Greece, and Turkey, with Greek-Cypriot and Turkish-Cypriot leaders, agreed terms for an independent bicommunal republic, barring both enosis and partition and naming the three powers as guarantors.

claims.title: Britain annexes Cyprus
claims.summary: After more than three centuries of Ottoman rule and thirty-six years of British administration, Britain annexes the island outright on entering the First World War against the Ottoman Empire.

claims.title: Independence of the Republic of Cyprus
claims.summary: Cyprus became an independent bicommunal republic under a power-sharing constitution, with Makarios III as president and Fazıl Küçük as Turkish-Cypriot vice-president, and Britain retaining sovereign base areas.

claims.title: Breakdown of power-sharing and intercommunal violence
claims.summary: After President Makarios proposed constitutional amendments curtailing Turkish-Cypriot safeguards, the partnership collapsed and intercommunal violence broke out; Turkish Cypriots withdrew from the bicommunal state into enclaves.

claims.title: UN peacekeeping force (UNFICYP) established
claims.summary: By Resolution 186 the UN Security Council created UNFICYP to prevent renewed fighting and restore normal conditions; the force has remained deployed in Cyprus ever since.

claims.title: Coup against Makarios
claims.summary: Greek-Cypriot nationalists in the National Guard, backed by the military junta in Athens, overthrew President Makarios in pursuit of enosis and installed Nikos Sampson.

claims.title: Turkish military intervention
claims.summary: Invoking its guarantor role under the 1960 treaty, Turkey landed forces in Cyprus; described by Turkey as a peace operation and by the Republic of Cyprus as an invasion, it ended with Turkish control of the northern third of the island.

claims.title: Turkish Federated State of Cyprus proclaimed
claims.summary: The Turkish-Cypriot leadership under Rauf Denktaş proclaimed a 'Turkish Federated State of Cyprus' in the north, presented as a building block for a future federation rather than a separate sovereign state.

claims.title: Security Council Resolution 353
claims.summary: The Council calls on all states to respect the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Cyprus, demands an immediate ceasefire and an end to foreign military intervention, and demands the withdrawal of foreign military personnel not authorised by international agreements.

claims.title: Declaration of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
claims.summary: The Turkish-Cypriot assembly under Rauf Denktaş unilaterally declared the independent Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in the island's north, presenting it as an act of self-determination.

claims.title: UN Security Council Resolution 541
claims.summary: The Security Council deplored the declaration, considered it legally invalid, called for its withdrawal, and called on all states not to recognise any Cypriot state other than the Republic of Cyprus.

claims.summary: The Security Council reaffirmed Resolution 541, condemned secessionist actions including the exchange of ambassadors with Turkey, and addressed the status of the fenced town of Varosha.

claims.title: The Committee on Missing Persons is established
claims.summary: The leaders of the two communities set up a bicommunal committee, with United Nations participation, to recover and identify the remains of the missing — a joint list of 2,002 people, 492 Turkish Cypriots and 1,510 Greek Cypriots.

claims.title: Crossing points open along the Green Line
claims.summary: For the first time in decades, crossing points in the UN buffer zone were opened, allowing movement between north and south and easing the communities' separation without settling the dispute.

claims.title: Annan Plan referendums fail
claims.summary: The UN reunification plan was approved by a majority of Turkish Cypriots but rejected by a large majority of Greek Cypriots in simultaneous referendums, so it was not implemented.

claims.title: Republic of Cyprus joins the European Union
claims.summary: Cyprus acceded to the EU as a divided island; EU law applies in full only in the south and is suspended in the north pending a political settlement.

claims.title: Crans-Montana talks collapse
claims.summary: UN-brokered reunification negotiations at Crans-Montana ended without agreement, after which Turkish-Cypriot leaders increasingly pressed for a two-state solution rejected by the Republic of Cyprus and the UN.
